newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down slightly on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down slightly on profit-taking.

text.p: Thai stocks closed slightly lower on Friday as investors sold mainly banks and took profits ahead of next week's release of first quarter earnings results of finance firms, brokers said.

"Investors decided to sell as they did not want to hold stocks over the weekend. At the same time others waited for the release of first quarter earnings of finance companies due to come out next week," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index closed 1.53 points lower at 700.23 on 3.4 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index shed 0.19 point to 53.29.
Decliners led gainers 137 to 129 while 119 issues remained unchanged.
Brokers said finance firms and banks, hit by slowing economic growth and increased provisioning requirements, were widely expected to report poor first quarter earnings.
"Foreigners were less active due to the closure of Singapore market today," Payuha said.
Most of the major sectors slipped on Friday. The banking sector ranked first in terms of value, falling 0.63 percent, followed by the commerce sector declining 4.48 percent.
Discount retailer Siam Makro topped the active list, falling seven baht to 67. Bangkok Bank shed four to 187.
Financially-troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce was up the daily 10 percent limit, rising 0.30 baht to four. On Thursday the stock lost over 75 percent of its value falling by up to 12 baht.
Gains in the bank came following remarks by the central bank on Thursday that its bailout plan for the institutiom might help prevent its shares from being delisted by the stock exchange.
